title: Ship of Theseus: When is it on longer your idea?
author: IoncedreamedisuckmyD
selftext:
This is both a question and a discussion.

For those that don’t know the ship of Theseus is “A thought experiment that raises the question of whether an object that has had all of its components replaced (specifically, a ship whose parts have all been replaced) remains fundamentally the same object. (Wikitionary)”

I’ve been wondering about this with AI assistance in game design. I don’t mind using or asking AI for ideas for simple concept builds for fun, but I’ve got a couple ideas I want to make that are very inspired and I want to treat them special. Problem is I hit roadblocks in figuring out certain core mechanics (how should this enemy behave? What should this setting be? Etc). 

I have refrained from using AI to answer such questions as I’ve felt it would make the ideas of the game not my own. The core and founding idea that inspired me to create this game could never be conceived by AI so on that I’m not worried. 

However, it’s tempting so I can move on in the design and building of the game.

comments.author: sirpalee
comments.body:
Think of it as being a lead software engineer or lead game designer at a studio. AI is not different from delegating some tasks to other people, and you making the decisions of what stays in and what gets thrown out.

Or the same as a movie directory. Denis Villeneuve gets the biggest credit for the Dune movies, yet hundreds or thousands of people contributed their own original ideas to the project.

replies.author: biocidebynight
replies.body:
Nailed it. Yeah, I am using clause code for my project, but my core vision is always the north star. I play more a role of project manager by delegating out the various work and checking each step to iterate towards that vision.

I do occasionally use AI for brainstorming, but it's always just a shotgun approach of just throwing shit out back and forth until I feel that we have something that matches the vision. 

There is almost nothing in my game that AI just "came up with". But, there are several little details that we workshopped together until it fit into the world/mechanics

replies.author: Trashy_io
replies.body:
Whenever I use AI for brainstorming and I usually give it a few good examples of the type of theme or feel I'm going for this usually helps out a lot with keeping the brain storming relative. But you guys are 100% right you should be acting as Project Manager/Director. 

With that being said, if you work on your understanding of AI/LLMs, as well as your understanding of each aspect of game development this will translate to less of a disconnect when trying to get your idea across and increase efficiency even more! 

All you have to understand is how AI likes to be talked to (prompt patterns), as well as the terminology for game development basically.

comments.author: HerbertGoon
comments.body: When you ask it for ideas

comments.author: CulturalFig1237
comments.body: This feels similar to using forums or books for inspiration, the intent and taste still come from you.

comments.author: Wobstep
comments.body:
Ai code assistance is a force multiplier. The same way a car can take you long distances much faster than walking. No matter if you walk or drive, you are still going to the same place. You didn't build the car or the roads but it wasn't someone else driving. 

Even without ai assistance, you are still developing with automated processes that you didn't build. Unless you make your own compiler, ide, language and all of the computer hardware, you can't say that you did it all on your own anyway. 

How many planks of a ship need to be replaced before it's no longer the same ship? It comes down to identity more than the actual specific material. As long as you curate the architecture, it doesn't really matter how the planks got to where they are.

replies.author: IoncedreamedisuckmyD
replies.body: I'm talking about for ideas and ideas on mechanics, not using it for code which I think is a great use of AI.
